payload.objective: Provide a read-only mathematical review of whether sequential per-token backward passes with detached frozen KV give the exact gradient of the summed per-token loss for this Gemma4 LoRA training design, and propose principled acceptance tests and tolerances.
payload.context: You are selected as the Sekhmet Akh listed in the durable fleet directory with model kimi-k3; Tecton is occupied by an older unrelated turn and has not started this request. Please begin your reply by confirming the actual model serving this turn (it must be Kimi K3; if it is not, say so and do not substitute an answer from another model) and include your runtime/session identifier if available. Setup: Gemma4, 48-layer causal decoder; only the final layer query projection has a rank-2 LoRA. Every other parameter, including every K/V projection, is frozen. LoRA dropout is zero and the model is in eval mode. Teacher-forced trajectories are collected and replayed under the same policy. Proposed update computes each target token loss sequentially with detached KV cache, calls backward per token to accumulate gradients, and performs exactly one optimizer step after the full eligible token bank. Review which parameter paths and hidden dependencies make that gradient mathematically equal to a full-prefix/full-sequence summed-loss gradient, and enumerate anything that invalidates it (including position/cache metadata, hybrid local/global attention, normalization, logits processing, stochasticity, mutable buffers, checkpointing/input gradients, loss normalization, and optimizer timing). Controls observed on a tiny FP32 instance of the actual architecture: hybrid-cached versus full-prefix logits agree and both nonzero LoRA gradients agree. In BF16, batched versus tokenwise arithmetic has a small 0.5625 maximum logit difference. Async CPU cache offload has an actual race and causes nondeterministic 22.5 maximum logit difference. Synchronous offload and resident-cache repeats are exact; cached-versus-full still has small BF16 rounding differences. Please separate acceptance criteria for: (1) mathematical gradient equivalence, (2) same-policy sampler/teacher-forced replay, (3) cache correctness and memory behavior, and (4) minibatch/summed objective equivalence. Recommend concrete metrics, reference constructions, repeated-run checks, and dtype/scale-aware tolerances. Specifically judge whether a universal raw max-logit BF16 gate of 1e-4 is invalid, and suggest a better gate. Relevant implementation facts: the engine disables gradient checkpointing and input-require-grad hooks, calls eval(), asserts the trainable surface contains only the selected LoRA projection, rejects cache tensors with requires_grad or grad_fn, records one optimizer step after the full bank, and describes cache transfer as synchronous caller stream when offloading. Additional control: async repeated-run delta is 19.9375 after restoring original Gemma arithmetic; GPU-resident and synchronous CPU-offload repeats are each exact, and resident equals synchronous; each differs from full-prefix BF16 by 0.5625. Both LoRA A/B gradients are nonzero. Treat the async race separately and do not loosen catastrophic-cache thresholds to cover it. No edits, deployment, credentials, or external actions are authorized; this is analysis only.

summary: Kimi K3 math review: exact LoRA gradients under detached KV replay
